content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text addresses the challenged Luke 2:48 phrase by immediate verse-level qualification rather than by weighing chain against chain by footing, so it is a K-C chain-collision ruling.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"\"the pressing side's own chain read together\" — I weighed whether C2's Luke 2:48-49 citation is a chain collision governed by K-C, or only a single-verse point outside K-C.","why":"The judge neutralizes Mary's phrase by immediate verse-level context instead of weighing the challenged chain against the defender's chain by footing, as K-C requires."}
